comments.value: I love this idea. Asset and Avatar stealing is def something VRC need to deal with, specially since you want to make a marketplace later down the line. This seems like an elegant solution if it can be made to work and secure.
Also when I mentioned whitelist/blacklist I didn't mean a list specifically but, more of something similar to the show/hide toggle.

This idea lack a severe volume of looking into the future and consiquences of that kind of system. I think it's easier if i break it into a few key Points:
1. First of all - what issue is that trying to prevent? "Not only would malicious users not see your main avatar upon initialization" - I think you mean this is suppose to prevent stealing of avatar? Sure, it will work in a short perspective, and your avatars will get some kind of safety, but, and only BUT from people not from your friends list, and the point where i'm going - what if your avatars will be stolen even after implimentaion? What are you gonna do THEN, delete hundreds of friends? And what if even that wont work, will you add those deleted friends back after finding out traitor? People, especially creators, will become extremely suspicious of whom they friend, i can't imagine how much of an anxiety that will give to them, to decide if it's safe to add a person or not, is he just pretending/pretended to be nice, but in reality - just want to steal my stuff?
2. Second point comes directly from first: if everybody(or most of the people) will have this feature on - what then? try to remember times when YOU guys started to play, were everyone Brushes and standart avatars? are YOU gonna add more friends, just from how they talk, without seeing their avatar at all? are YOU gonna be happy, to come to a friend and see 10 standart avatars, and only 2 of your friends? This will destroy the whole point of vrchat - meeting people, and connecting to them, when everybody have a special personality - their avatars. You said the feture should be by deafulte off, but you just place people in a position where they can either "be safe" and their avatar won't be stolen, or they can risk and meet new people, ask yourself - what will you choose, and how many NEW friends (especially considering first point and suspicious, or anxiety of avatar safety) will you add in a future with that system?(and yes, i assume that MOST of people are not using custom fallbacks, since creaton of such takes tons of effort, and avatar creators will not provide them with main avatar, at least not without additional payment)
3. What about perfomance result of that? how much of a personal, server and internet speed perfomance will that take? additional checks  and requests, potential to abuse, since, if you switch that constantly - people on others side they will have to load you fallback, then normal avatar, and then back in a circles few times a second, how to prevent that?
And surely some stuff i forgot, but in general - System like that has a potential to destroy current social system, break already established connections between people and ruin ways to make new friends, without providing any replacement, ask yourself - is it really worth, especially considering it's not even giving you a 100% safety from a problem you're trying to solve in a first place?
P.S. I'm sure that avatar and assets stealing is a problem that has to be solved, especially considering incoming economy system, but that surely not the way for it.

@{5f316ea23621ce4fdf77ca93|full_name}: These points are very much vaild and I appreciate your input on this. This is definitely something that has slipped by in this suggestion. Given the nature of VRC was to be a social platforms to let people find friends and such, this system would create a high gate/barrier for people to befriend each other. 
But I would also like to think this is where the trusted rank system would be a great help. Much like to the current safety settings, this system can be toggled off for certain ranks of users to lower the barriers between users and the social aspects. The one of the biggest purpose on this system is to significantly reduce the possiblities of avatar rippers and theives in VRChat. And to my experience, large ratio of these rippers are either below the rank of trusted users (orange). 
Now, there is no doubt that the possibilties of a ripper being one of your friend or a high trust rank user, But the numbers of these rippers will be far more less than what we have now. Thats why the report system would still exist. We are aware that it is almost imposible to get rid of ALL avatar creators. But this would help the morderation team to reduce weight and numbers of cases to where if a report was submitted, They will be able to start the investigation in a greater efficiency. 
Again I really appreciate the thoughts and vaild points given here, this is why this canny post was made and I happy to see people are giving this a piece of their mind.

@{5fb7b65f52f1f5365d7c9f67|full_name}: @{5f316ea23621ce4fdf77ca93|full_name}'s second point is very strong in my opinion. While i personally think, something should be done about avatar security, one should try not to be too restrictive in regards of what people can see or not.
"And to my experience, large ratio of these rippers are either below the rank of trusted users (orange). "
My experience is the other way around. Especially since they seem to have found a way to make them known/trusted almost immediatelly after account creating.
---
But back to topic.
You have to look into the process of avatar ripping and make it more laborious, so that the amount of work people have to put into repairing/reuploading would make it not worth anymore. Also unintentionall access should be restricted, which adds even more "work" to access avatars directly. But ultimately, you cannot make an avatar "unrippable", since at some point is has to be displayable by your graphics cards, which means at this point you could potentially rip it from the gpus vram.
About blacklist:
if we could manually create a blacklist for people which are not allowed to load our avatars/worlds like you suggested with black/whitelisting in general could be nice. So whenever i would come around someone who is a ripper, that i can warn friends etc so they could update their lists. But this could potentially lead to missuse as well. It is a difficult topic to rightfully judge someone if he/she is a definitive ripper or not.

I think the developers have said they won't do this because of some social problems they just made up, similar to how Tupper said scaling would create social problems in a what if situation he just made up in his head that doesn't exist.
Would be really good for safety and would make publics safer for people using custom avatars, as long as the avatar doesn't download on their end even though your safety is enabled to not show for random people.

details:
I was discussing with a friend regarding people hotswapping/ripping avatars and they thought of an idea that could help mitigate future spread of this issue, revitalize publics and MAYBE put an end to the future of ripperstore (an asset redistributing website filled with stolen avatars).
Think of this, let's say there was a fallback system like what we currently have but for nonfriends or non whitelisted users. People would have their main avatars viewable to specifically friends and whitelisted users whilst others would see a chosen avatar we selected? Not only would malicious users not see your main avatar upon initialization but would also allow users to selectively choose who they want to view it. Furthermore, it could allow people to join their friends in publics without the whole switching to a disposable model every time and the hassle behind it. It would also prevent friends of friends of friends from joining and just yoinking your avatar, Friends+ would no longer just be a a discount public lobby/random gateway for people to join and could be safe aswell. I've had my avatars stolen countless of times without even stepping a foot in public. I'm seeing this from a avatar creator perspective and I hope other creators would agree with me. Asset stealing is a HUGE issue in VRChat and we definitely need a way to atleast mitigate or slow down the process behind this. I've known multiple people around the community who's gotten their days/months work stolen from in a blink of an eye and reuploaded publicly. This feature could also alleviate stress on the support team, all of the previous features are already implemented (Fallback avatars, safety, whitelist/blacklist) but I think this could be a valid security feature on top of that. And with the announcement of the VRC avatar economy I think this should be a priority and there is absolutely no doubt in my mind a NEED for avatar security before anything gets implemented. 
***This feature could be disabled by default to prevent new users who arent familiar with the system to not question why other users don't see their avatars.***
I would love to hear what the community thinks of the idea.
Thank you
title: New fallback avatar security system for mitigating theft
